history.title: Brief History of Tagaytay City
history.charteredDesc: Tagaytay is one of the Philippines' earliest chartered cities, established under Commonwealth Act No. 338 by President Manuel L. Quezon.
history.elevationDesc: Tagaytay sits atop a ridge at approximately 600–700 meters above sea level, giving it one of the coolest climates in Luzon and the iconic Taal Volcano views.

precolonial.title: Tagalog Settlements
precolonial.text: Tagaytay ridge inhabited by the Tagalog people; the elevated terrain overlooking Taal Lake served as a natural vantage point and fertile agricultural land.

spanish.title: Spanish Era
spanish.text: Spanish missionaries establish settlements along Cavite's highland regions. Tagaytay area becomes part of the Cavite encomienda system under colonial administration.

charter.title: City Charter
charter.text: Commonwealth Act No. 338 signed by President Manuel L. Quezon on July 27, 1938, constituting Tagaytay as a city — one of the earliest chartered cities in the Philippines.

summer.title: Summer Capital
summer.text: Tagaytay designated as the 'Summer Capital of the Philippines' due to its cool climate, scenic mountain air, and panoramic views of Taal Volcano and Lake.

capital.title: Capital Proposal
capital.text: The Marcos administration considers relocating the national capital to Tagaytay. The proposal, driven by its strategic elevation and climate, was ultimately not pursued.

eruption.title: Taal Eruption
eruption.text: Taal Volcano erupts on January 12, 2020, prompting mass evacuation of Tagaytay City residents and temporarily closing down the city's vital tourism sector.

leadership.title: New Leadership & Recovery
leadership.text: Mayor Aizack Brent D. Tolentino elected. The city continues recovery and development of tourism infrastructure, including completion of the world-class Tagaytay City Velodrome.
